Consultant's visit by Flora 03052016
Campus Location
Shrewsbury School is situated in Shrophire, to the northwest of Birmingham. As there is no direct train service to this location, one has to change train in Birmingham in order to get there. The train journey takes about 2 hours 45 mins. To reach the toun centre, however a 10 mins walk is required from Shrewsbury train station, whereas a 15 mins ride by taxi is needed in order to get from Shrewsbury train station to the institute.

Campus

-150 acres, red bricked buildings, lots of greens

Accommodation
A total of 9 boarding houses and 2 day houses can be found within the school campus. I was taken on a tour to the “School House” right next to the main school. The boarding house system is described as a vertical one which implies that one can find all year groups boarders under the same roof.
The school house can accommodate a total of 84 boarders spreading over a building 5 storeys high.
	
For lower form boarders, they can share a room with a minimum of two and a maximum of 5 occupants. No desk can be found in the room however to ensure that studying activities are confined to the study room. In order words, the sleeping room sole purpose is only meant for resting. 
The 6th formers, nonetheless, are entitled to have the privileges of staying alone in single rooms of their own. They enjoy more privacy.

I was also shown to a place called” Emma Darwin Hall” which incidentally is a boarding house for girls. Everything there was nice, brand new and modern. Here, one can enjoy the convenience of having desks to work and above all, elevators for climbing staircases instead. 

Facilities

- The resourceful library is well-stocked with materials of all kinds of tranquil and cosy environment make one feels like reading at home. 
- The Economics and Science building is a newly completed classroom block which looks a bit more modern in comparison to the order surrounding building complex.
- Sport is highly valued here in Shrewsbury School. Football is the most popular sport pursued by the majority of the students who find it most enjoyable with the numerous up-dated facilities available. 
Rowing has become a big sport here at Shrewsbury School too. The rowing teams here as can be expected, quite sizable in nature.
Other sports like Rugby, netball, fencing, badminton, basketball, rickets, and hockey also constitute part of the regular school curriculum. 
There is also an indoor swimming pool and a gym to cater for the needs of those who care to shape –up their bodies.
-A new design and technology centre was opened in September 2016 within the school campus. The building is new and modern with plenty of pupils’ works. Good DT!
-In addition, a new academic hall has recently been put into service as well. (just opened in 2015)
-Standard of Art is really impressive. Exhibits of the pupils’ Art works are displayed for appreciation.
-The school chapel is well-decorated with tinted-glasses, which makes the whole place look solemn yet colourful. 
-Pupils have their meals at a central dining hall. (I had my lunch there, foods-wide range, taste ok…)
- School will provide coach service for international students with small fees from Heathrow to Shrewsbury School on the first day/last day of term. 

General

-	6th formers can choose their tutor by their own tutor by their own, good relationship between tutors and students ie they go cinema, students will go to tutor’s house to sleepover, they meet at least 3-4 times a week

Although the school doesn't has spectacular buildings.  I can feel the teachers have heart to teach and respect students a lot too.

Campus Location:
The nearest station of the school is Godalming. It is about less than an hour from London Waterloo.

Campus
The school occupies a large site in excess of 200 acres and located on the slope. The original neo-Gothic school building comprises the four ‘old houses’ and the eight ‘new houses’ . 

Accommodation:
Students are divided amongst the twelve boarding Houses. The original three – Saunderites, Verites and Gownboys (where scholar lives and entitled to wear gown), known as the Block Houses, together with one other, Girdlestoneites – are grouped at the centre of the School and are collectively known as the ‘Old’ Houses. 
Seven Houses – Lockites, Weekites, Hodgsonites, Daviesites, Bodeites, Pageites and Robinites are called the ‘New’ Houses.  
A sixth form House, Fletcherites, is opened in 2010. Fletcherites is a mixed boarding House for sixth formers only and all the First Year Specialists (Year 12) in this House are new to the School. The boys and girls have shared common rooms and other facilities, with separate residential accommodation.

The other eleven Houses have sixth form year groups of approximately two thirds boys and one third girls. The girls spend the working day as an integral part of their House and return to their Halls of Residence at the end of the evening
Students have their lunch and dinner at school in the central dining hall.

Facilities:
The sporting facilities are impressive and include: the Queen's Sports Centre; athletics track; three all weather Astro pitches; flood lit tennis courts; fives, racquets and squash courts; and The Halford Hewitt Golf Course. The Halford Hewitt Golf Course is a 9-hole, par 34 course occupying approximately 30 acres of the Charterhouse campus. The Queen's Sports Centre has an indoor swimming pool, multi-use sports hall, climbing wall and a well-equipped fitness gym. Art Center and Music block are very outstanding as well. Pupils regularly perform in ten minute recitals during quarter (the morning break), and there is a host of choirs and ensembles: Chapel Choir, Chamber Choir, Symphony Orchestra, String Orchestra, Jazz Band and Brass Ensemble and Concert Band. School Shop and School Library are huge. Students can visit the library anytime and opened till night time.

Suitable For:
Students who are looking for traditional school.
All-rounded and outgoing students with good academic result.
Wide interests and willing to commit and participate in different sports and music activities.

Shy students, only focus on work, not sociable

20221124: From Helen

Just thought I would send you a summary of my visit to Sedbergh School yesterday.  It is actually 10 years since I was last at the school and it was good to meet up with a few familiar faces.  David Milner, the Director of Marketing & Admissions , met me when I arrived and I then had a meeting with the Deputy Head, Dr Jenny Burns, who joined the school in 2021 from Durham School.  The Headmaster sent his best wishes and was sorry he wouldn’t see me but he was in London at a fundraising event.

Two Hong Kong pupils accompanied me on a tour of the school.  Fione and Isaac are both 14 years old and joined the school last year in Year 9.  Fione is a little quiet but a very nice girl and she particularly enjoys her Art and Design - told me she would probably stay for the Sixth Form and she seems happy and settled.  Isaac seemed a bit more ambitious and very confident – he said his mother is a Barrister and his father a Specialist Surgeon – he said he would probably go on to another more academic school for the Sixth Form which was interesting.  Fione’s three words to sum up the school were:  Family/Sporty/Tiring and Isaac’s were:  Family/Care/Sympathy.  Good to see that they both said Family and I do think this could partly be because the school has retained the house dining system – there are only five schools left with this system in the UK as it is much more expensive than having central feeding.  I do feel it does, however, create a family atmosphere when you have all your meals in your boarding house.

It was raining quite heavy during my tour and I did not see as much as I would have liked.  The sports facilities are very good and the Hurst Centre that was opened three years ago has a multi-functional sports hall that converts for formal occasions and has seating for 1,000 – it also houses a fitness centre and very nice hospitality facilities.  The next major development is a Design/Computing and Technology Centre which will be built for September 2025.  The main school building has been refurbished and there is a very nice entrance and reception area for visitors.  The general classroom areas that I visited remain very much the same.  I only visited the communal areas of one of the boys houses which has had some refurbishment but did not see any bedrooms.  I had lunch on one of the girls houses and the food was good – I did ask to see some of the girls bedrooms and they are fine but I did think they were particularly messy and untidy.  I have read the Inspection Report from February this year and the school meets all the necessary regulations but interestingly states that the boarding accommodation is “adequate”.  I did speak to David Milner about this when I met him for coffee before I left.  I told him that I had recommended the refurbishment of the boys houses 10 years ago – he said that work was very much ongoing but with such large properties that were constantly in use it was a long process.  I asked him to send me some images as I had not seen any of the rooms during my tour.

The school is doing well and the boarding houses are full – they have been granted an increase in their numbers for next year.  I really did not see any other pupils from China as I toured the school and Fione and Isaac are the only ones from Asia on their houses.  I feel that the main reason for this, especially for the market, is that Sedbergh is still not recognised as an academic school and pupils really do need to want to embrace sport and outdoor life as part of their education.  I did discuss this with David and he fully understands.  The positive is that at the weekends the school remains full and very busy – they have refused to go down the flexi/weekly boarding route and it does seem to have paid off.  Out of 550 pupils, they only have 20 day pupils and they are the children of staff and some local scholars from the State schools in the area.

Sedbergh would really like to be part of the next physical  AA event and they have built up a good reputation for their sport in HK.   I said I would pass on this message to you and they said they would be thrilled if they were invited.  For HK families with very bright, studious children Sedbergh is not an option.  If there are families, however, with children who enjoy their sport and the outdoors and are average academically then they would certainly be getting a British boarding school experience and plenty of fresh air!!  Interesting to note that Fione said her parents chose Sedbergh so she would have the opportunity to be much more active than she had been in HK and she would be more healthy.  Isaac also said that he thought he was a bit of a wimp before joining Sedbergh and he now felt more resilient after being so active!

In summary, Sedbergh is a very busy bustling school but I still maintain that it is best suited to students who have quite strong personalities and who enjoy being very active.  I think it is quite a hard environment and more gentle students might struggle with the rough and tumble.  The housemistress that I had lunch with was going wild water swimming in the afternoon (in November!!) with pupils – I rest my case!!!!!!!!
